Computation controls for the session or for one call

Source: R/estimate_control.R
control_computation.Rd

The computation controls say how the draws of a model or a test run, not what is fitted: seed, ncores, and strategy. They are the same for every model, so they can persist across the scripts of a session.

  • set_control_computation() writes them to options(snet_computation), after it checks them. Each later call of estimate_mrqap(), test_random(), test_configuration(), test_permutation(), test_gof(), test_distributions(), test_parameter(), test_time(), and play_diffusions() then uses them where they are not given, and says so with options(snet_verbosity = "verbose"). {goldfish} reads the same option.

  • control_computation() gives them to one call only, as control = c(control_mrqap(...), control_computation(...)), or control = control_computation(...) alone.

A control given in a call, such as control_mrqap(seed = 1) or control = list(seed = 1), takes priority. Then comes control_computation(), then options(snet_computation), and then the default of control_mrqap().

set_control_computation() changes only the controls that it is given. A control given as NULL is removed, and persist = FALSE removes all of them. The option is checked again when it is read, since it can also be set by hand.

A persistent seed sets the same seed in every call, so each call draws the same random numbers, sequentially or in parallel, and its result can be reproduced. The print of a result gives the seed that it used, and every result records its controls as control.

Usage

set_control_computation(
  seed = NULL,
  ncores = NULL,
  strategy = NULL,
  persist = TRUE
)

control_computation(seed = NULL, ncores = NULL, strategy = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'mrqap_control'
c(...)

Arguments

seed

A number to set the random seed with before the draws. See control_mrqap().

ncores

A whole number of cores to run the draws on. See control_mrqap().

strategy

The {future} plan that the draws run on where ncores is NULL: "sequential", "multisession", "multicore", or "cluster". See control_mrqap().

persist

Logical. TRUE (the default) writes the controls that are given to the option. FALSE clears the option, and takes no controls.

...

For c(), the result of control_mrqap() and then of control_computation().

Value

set_control_computation() returns the value of options(snet_computation) before the call, invisibly, so that options(snet_computation = old) restores it. control_computation() returns an object of class infernetComputationControl: a list of the controls that it is given.

See also

Other estimating functions: control_mrqap(), other_results, print.infernetMrqapFit()

Examples

# For the session: later calls use these where they are not given
old <- set_control_computation(seed = 1, ncores = 1)
control_mrqap()
#> # Controls for an MRQAP: 2 set, 13 at their defaults
#> 
#>   seed    1  (option)
#>   ncores  1  (option)
#> 
#> # (option) persists from set_control_computation();
#> #   set_control_computation(persist = FALSE) clears it.
# A control given in a call wins
control_mrqap(seed = 2)$seed
#> [1] 2
# NULL removes one control, and persist = FALSE removes all of them
set_control_computation(ncores = NULL)
getOption("snet_computation")
#> $seed
#> [1] 1
#> 
set_control_computation(persist = FALSE)
options(snet_computation = old)

# For one call only
control_computation(seed = 3)
#> # Computation controls for one call: 1 set
#> 
#>   seed  3
c(control_mrqap(family = "poisson"), control_computation(seed = 3))
#> # Controls for an MRQAP: 2 set, 13 at their defaults
#> 
#>   family  "poisson"
#>   seed    3
